Metadata.title: Aegis — Content safety platform
Metadata.description: Text and image content safety, policy rules, workflow orchestration, and release governance for enterprise teams. This prototype uses simulated moderation results.

Site.footerBlurb: A prototype content safety platform for rules, workflows, model capabilities, and release governance.
Site.rights: Prototype interface. Not a production service.

Home.title: Moderate content, govern policy, and release with a traceable version.
Home.subtitle: Aegis gives enterprise teams one place to test text and image safety, configure rules, orchestrate workflows, and review simulated release decisions.
Home.mockNotice: Public testing uses simulated decisions. Results are marked as demo output and are not model judgments.
Home.capabilitiesIntro: The prototype separates detection, policy, orchestration, and release so each can evolve on its own.

capabilities.title: Text moderation
capabilities.description: Check user text against demo scenes and return allow, block, review, or a service error.

capabilities.title: Image moderation
capabilities.description: Preview a local image, validate type and size, and show a simulated image decision.

capabilities.title: Rules and policy
capabilities.description: Create keyword, ignore-term, regex, structured, and model-threshold rules with versions.

capabilities.title: Visual workflows
capabilities.description: Connect start, rules, branches, model calls, merge, and end nodes on a canvas.

capabilities.title: Model capabilities
capabilities.description: Register simulated platform capabilities. The catalog does not call a live model.

capabilities.title: Decision trace
capabilities.description: Keep the final decision separate from timeouts and service failures.

capabilities.title: Evaluation and release
capabilities.description: Run a mirror evaluation and a baseline regression before a simulated publish or rollback.

stages.title: Read the exchange
stages.body: Text, images, and model output enter one surface, with the application and channel attached.

stages.title: Judge it against policy
stages.body: Rules, labels, and model scores produce one of three outcomes: allow, block, or human review.

stages.title: Enforce before it ships
stages.body: The decision is returned to the product. A failed check stays an error and never becomes an allow.

Products.title: What the platform is responsible for
Products.description: Detection, policy, orchestration, and release stay in separate modules. This page describes the prototype, not a live production deployment.

items.title: Moderation APIs

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: The public docs describe the example moderation contract. They do not require a login.

sections.title: What you can call
paragraphs: The prototype documents POST /v1/moderation/text and POST /v1/moderation/image.
Both return the same decision envelope.

sections.title: How the product is split
paragraphs: Rules manage policy. Workflows decide the order of checks. The capability center registers models. A merge policy produces allow, block, or review.
A service error is not turned into a decision.

sections.title: Demo boundary
paragraphs: Responses in this website set is_mock to true. The playground does not call a hosted model.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.description: Use these steps to read the contract. The host api.example.com is illustrative.

sections.title: 1. Choose an endpoint
paragraphs: Use the text endpoint for a string and the image endpoint for an image reference.

sections.title: 2. Understand authentication
paragraphs: A future server will require a bearer token. The sample value is YOUR_API_KEY.

sections.title: 3. Build and send a request
paragraphs: Send JSON with a scene id. The playground uses the same text fields.

sections.title: 4. Read the response
paragraphs: When status is success, decision is allow, block, or review. When status is error, decision is null.

sections.title: 5. Handle errors
paragraphs: Branch on status before reading decision. Do not treat an error as allow.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.description: Production calls should use a server-side credential. This site does not contain a real key.

sections.title: Credential model
paragraphs: The planned API authenticates with a bearer token issued on the server. Browser apps should call your own backend, not store a secret.

sections.title: Example header
paragraphs: Replace the placeholder only on a server you control.

sections.title: Placeholder only
paragraphs: YOUR_API_KEY is not a credential. The console does not issue keys in this prototype.

text-moderation.title: Text moderation
text-moderation.description: POST /v1/moderation/text checks a string and returns the shared envelope.

sections.title: Endpoint
paragraphs: Method: POST. Path: /v1/moderation/text. Body: JSON.

sections.title: Fields
paragraphs: text is the content. scene_id selects a configured scene. metadata.source identifies the caller, such as playground.

sections.title: Example
paragraphs: The review sample below is the canonical example used across the site.

sections.title: Errors
paragraphs: An empty body or a string over the shared character limit returns 400. Rate limiting returns 429. A dependency outage returns 503 and no decision.

image-moderation.title: Image moderation
image-moderation.description: POST /v1/moderation/image describes the future image contract. The playground never uploads the file.

sections.title: Endpoint
paragraphs: Method: POST. Path: /v1/moderation/image.

sections.title: Input methods
paragraphs: The documented JSON input is an image_url. A future multipart upload can send the bytes to your server.
The playground reads the file locally, checks type and size, and discards it when you leave the page.

sections.title: Example
paragraphs: Limits below come from the same configuration as the playground.

sections.title: Data handling
paragraphs: Do not send secrets in image metadata. A production proxy must limit size, type, rate, and retention before any model sees the file.

errors.title: Error codes
errors.description: These codes are the prototype contract. Confirm them with the backend before a production launch.

sections.title: Catalog
paragraphs: An error response uses status error. It does not include a moderation decision.

sections.title: Do not coerce errors
paragraphs: A timeout or a 503 must stay an error. It must not be stored as allow, block, or review.

Console.title: Operations console
Console.subtitle: Internal prototype
Console.accessNotice: This console is a prototype. A signed-in tenant filter runs in the browser and is not server isolation or authorization.
Console.overviewBody: Rules, workflows, capabilities, evaluations, and releases are separate records. Counts come from the prototype store on this server and stay in sync with this browser.
Console.rulesBoundaryBody: Rules define a match and a recommended action. Editing a published rule creates a candidate version.
Console.workflowBoundaryBody: A workflow orders rule checks, model calls, branches, and a merge. A valid graph is not an approval to publish.
Console.decisionBoundaryBody: The merge policy returns allow, block, or review. Timeouts stay errors and do not become decisions.
Console.queueSample: A community post asks for a policy check before it is shown to other members.
Console.inquiriesBody: Sales contact and access requests from the public site are stored on this server and stay visible here after a refresh.

Workflows.title: Workflows
Workflows.description: The example graph runs a rule, branches, optionally calls a simulated model, merges the result, and ends. Nothing here calls a production model.
Workflows.newDescription: Start connected to end. Add the other nodes before publishing.
Workflows.name: Name
Workflows.forkedHelp: The published graph was not overwritten.
Workflows.saveFailed: The workflow could not be saved
Workflows.selectNode: Select a node to edit it. Drag between handles to connect. Press Delete to remove a selected node or edge.
Workflows.simNotice: The run is a local simulation. A timeout stays an error and does not become allow, block, or review.
Workflows.resultError: The run did not produce a decision
Workflows.branchHelp: Connect the upper handle to the matched path and the lower handle to the missed path. Only the listed fields and operators are available.

block_first.label: Block first
block_first.help: If any input is block, the result is block. Otherwise review wins over allow.

priority.label: First decision
priority.help: Keep the earliest decision in execution order. A rule hit is used before a later model result.

conflict_review.label: Conflict to review
conflict_review.help: If allow and block are both present, the result is review. Otherwise block wins, then review, then allow.
